printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), smooth PEI sheet
derived_from: two-colour-planned-change, a black-white-black box printed with two planned colour changes: its G-code with the first change's colour renamed red, and one of its own frames, unaltered
part: a 20 x 20 x 12 mm open-topped box with 10% infill, in PLA: black to Z 4, then white from Z 4, as printed
verdict: derived failure: the spool loaded at a planned change is the wrong colour, 2.8 mm of white where the G-code plans red, seen only on the whole frame a stale calibration gives

fault.kind: a wrong spool loaded at a planned colour change
fault.how: fault.diff renames the slice's first planned change, at layer 20 (Z 4), from #FFFFFF to #FF0000 on its `;COLOR_CHANGE` line, the one line it changes, so every byte position stays the print's. The G-code then plans red from Z 4 to its change back to #000000 at layer 40 (Z 8), while the frame shows the white a person loaded there

what_it_looks_like: the box's low walls black to Z 4 and plainly white above, 2.8 mm up to the frame's Z 6.8, with its open cross-hatched infill, beside the head at the sheet's centre; the camera has moved since its calibration, so the check is handed the whole frame

expected_agent_action.operation: pause, or acknowledge the check as watch
expected_agent_action.why: the skill holds a whole frame's colour as no grounds to pause until new layers since the change pass 5 mm, because on this print's whole frames the thin new black after the second change reads as white and was paused on as a wrong colour; the white here is 2.8 mm, so the case documents a plain-frame wrong spool without claiming it is caught below 5 mm: a pause or a watch is accepted, and cancelling or adjusting anything never is. The wrong band ends at the second planned change at Z 8, 4 mm above the first, so no frame of this print shows it past 5 mm

frames.label: layer 14, Z 2.8, black, a minute before the planned change at Z 4: the print head stands over the centre of the sheet and hides the small black box under it; healthy. A byte-for-byte copy of ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-133618-obs-l14.jpg.

layer 24, Z 4.8, four layers past the planned change at Z 4: the server's check as the print carries on from it; the head stands over the part and hides it, so its new colour cannot be seen. A byte-for-byte copy of ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-134200-resumed-white-l24.jpg.

layer 34, Z 6.8: the box in view beside the head, black low walls under 2.8 mm of plainly white walls with open cross-hatched infill, in its place at the sheet's centre; the slice this case plants names red from Z 4, so the white is a defect. A byte-for-byte copy of ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-134401-obs-white-l34.jpg.

sources.gcode: the printed G-code is ../two-colour-planned-change/two-colour-box.gcode with fault.diff applied: the diff is committed alone, and the replay makes the file from that G-code
sources.frames: frame-133618-p25.2.jpg, frame-134200-p34.1.jpg and frame-134401-p44.7.jpg are ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-133618-obs-l14.jpg, ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-134200-resumed-white-l24.jpg and ../two-colour-planned-change/agent-134401-obs-white-l34.jpg

scenarios.summary: A periodic observation at layer 14 in the black, a minute before the printer reaches its first planned colour change, with the head hiding the part; the agent should carry on and change nothing.

The server's check as the print carries on from the planned change at Z 4, which names red; the head hides the part, so its new colour cannot be seen yet; the agent may carry on, or pause if it already sees the wrong colour.

A periodic observation on the whole frame shows the box's new layers plainly white from the planned change at Z 4, 2.8 mm of them, where the G-code names red; below 5 mm of new layers a whole frame's colour is no grounds to pause, so the agent may pause or watch, and never cancels or adjusts.
